newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen pausing after new record rise.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen pausing after new record rise.

text.p: Belgian stocks could trade sideways on Tuesday after breaking new records on Monday in a session dominated by another bout of bank merger fever, traders and analysts said.
"I would like the market to consolidate, as it did on Friday, for a few days. It needs it," Gert De Mesure of Antwerp brokerage Delen & Co said.

"If you look elsewhere in Europe and after the Dutch rate hike it could be time to take some profits in equities," a trader at a Ghent-based brokerage added. "But it's difficult to say when, when we have new records every day."
The Dutch central bank on Monday raised its central money market rate to 2.90 percent from 2.70 percent -- its second rate hike in a month aimed at countering weakness in the guilder.
But the move left the bluechip Bel-20 Index largely unscathed. The index ended up 0.89 percent at a new closing high of 2,205.20 points.

The index was supported by heavy buying of bank shares following renewed talk of a link between Generale Bank and BBL. Dealers said banks launching new Bel-20-linked funds were also buyers of all the shares that make up the index.

Philippe Liotier, chief executive officer Societe Generale de Belgique was quoted in an interview with an investor magazine as saying SGB was still interested in a link between its Generale Bank unit and BBL.
Generale Bank's share ended up 4.96 percent at 13,750 francs on the news, despite a later SGB statement that no talks were underway. BBL added another 1.4 percent to 8,200 francs.

Rival Kredietbank also rose despite the fact it is largely sidelined by the machinations surrounding BBL's shareholdership. KB shares, helped by buying of "baskets" of shares in the Bel-20 index, rose 1.7 percent to 13,125 francs.

De Mesure said he believed a merger in the sector was almost certainly on the cards, especially since Dexia CC, one of BBL's main shareholders, was now a publicly quoted company in its own right and focusing on its own alliance with Credit Local de France.
"Something has to happen with these banks and/or a foreign bank. The only question is when and with who," De Mesure said.
However, traders said the bank shares could also be suffering from "buy on rumour, sell on fact" expectations ahead of the release of earnings figures this week.
Generale Bank is due to report late on Tuesday. Kredietbank follows on Thursday. BBL released its figures last week.
"Generale Bank is looking expensive, although if a merger did happen we would have a great company," one trader said.
SGB's share fell in heavy volume on the bank merger talk, ending down 0.52 percent at 2,880 francs. Liotier was quoted as saying he believed the share was undervalued.
